html:
SMTO-SKL-0019 — SMTO couldn't prepare this calendar request

GUID: bc05a0fa-93ad-5d61-9e0b-bd9388c6be00
Slug: google-calendar-invalid-arguments
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • The details of this calendar request didn't fit together, so SMTO stopped before changing anything. For example, an edit didn't say what to change, or a guest was listed twice.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask again and name the calendar, the event (with its date and time) and exactly what should change, such as the title, time or guests. An edit with no clear change, or an event SMTO can't identify exactly, is refused.
  2. If you're adding guests, list each email address only once. SMTO rejects a guest list with the same person twice.
  3. If you're moving an event, choose a different calendar from the one it's in now. Special events such as out-of-office or focus time can't be moved. Google only allows moving regular events between two different calendars.
  4. Don't ask SMTO to delete your main Google calendar. Delete individual events or a calendar you created instead. SMTO never deletes your main calendar, to protect everything in it.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the request and the change shows in Google Calendar.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; they show which part of the request was refused.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Calendar argument validation rejected the operation: arguments fail the tool's JSON schema, an unsafe calendar_id or path, singleEvents=false with orderBy=startTime, duplicate attendees, conflicting reminders, an update or move with no supported change, or a delete of the primary calendar.

What this means

  • Calendar operation validation rejects schema fields, unsafe provider paths, incompatible ordering, duplicate attendees or an update with no supported changed field. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Calendar operation validation rejects schema fields, unsafe provider paths, incompatible ordering, duplicate attendees or an update with no supported changed field.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact schema or operation-specific condition and required ETag/send_updates fields.

How to fix it

  • Compare the call with the discovered google_calendar tool schema: use exact provider calendar and event IDs, explicit send_updates for changes, and the event's observed ETag for existing events. Remove duplicate attendee emails, don't combine use_default reminders with overrides, supply at least one changed field, and don't move to the same calendar, move non-default event types or delete the primary calendar.
  • Use the discovered structured tool schema and exact provider IDs. Supply explicit send_updates for mutations and an observed ETag for existing events.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use the discovered structured tool schema and exact provider IDs. Supply explicit send_updates for mutations and an observed ETag for existing events.

How to verify the fix

  • Correct structured arguments pass local validation before the intended provider request.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
